summary: Iteration 912 TARGETED RETEST of BUG2 only. Applied fix (ScrollView key={currentStep}) is in the deployed static bundle (index-05cc83dafc8bcce026152e33e44cb2ea.js, mtime 23:41 > src 23:15). Reproduced the full free-user flow @1920x1080: login (p1.free.1779113329@example.com), cleared travel-visa-onboarding-complete localStorage, /features/travel-visa, step1 US, step2 tourist, step3. RESULT: BUG2 STILL FAILING ❌ — level cards render at getBoundingClientRect().y = -234 (offscreen above viewport, w=305 each, 3-column layout is correct: xs=480/797/1115, ys all=-234). The `key={currentStep}` remount fix on the INNER onboarding ScrollView is INEFFECTIVE. TRUE ROOT CAUSE (identified via full ancestry chain DOM inspection this iteration): the OUTER TravelVisaMain ScrollView `[data-testid="tv-v2-root"]` (ancestor level 9) has scrollTop=564 at step 3, AND has `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` on itself. RN-Web applies this identity transform to every ScrollView. Per CSS spec, any transformed ancestor establishes a NEW containing block for descendant position:fixed elements — so `tv-v2-onboarding-overlay` (position:fixed, top:0) is captured by tv-v2-root and TRANSLATED UP by tv-v2-root.scrollTop=564. That is why the overlay body is at y=-437 in the DOM despite being 'fixed'. Confirmed: after JS-forcing document.querySelector('[data-testid="tv-v2-root"]').scrollTop=0 at step 3, the beginner card jumps from y=-234 to y=330 — VISIBLE. Only 1 ancestor with scrollTop>0 was found (the tv-v2-root itself). The iter_911 fix does not touch this outer scroller.

ui_bugs.issue: Level cards render at y=-234 (offscreen) at step 3. Root cause: the OUTER `tv-v2-root` ScrollView on TravelVisaMain has scrollTop=564 and an identity `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` (added by react-native-web on every ScrollView). Because ANY transformed ancestor establishes a new containing block for position:fixed descendants, the onboarding overlay (position:fixed top:0, correctly authored) is captured by tv-v2-root and dragged 564px UP with its scroll. The iter_911 `key={currentStep}` fix on the INNER ScrollView is orthogonal — it only remounts a nested scroller that already had scrollTop=0 anyway. Proof: (a) full ancestry chain shows only tv-v2-root has scrollTop>0 (=564); (b) after forcing tv-v2-root.scrollTop=0 via JS, beginner card moves from y=-234 to y=330 (visible). Real free users still see a blank overlay with only Back/Get Started buttons at step 3.

integration_issues.issue: Cannot complete onboarding via visible UI — level cards are entirely above viewport. Get Started button remains disabled. Flow only completable by scripted click.

action_items: PRIMARY FIX (recommended): Render the TravelVisaOnboarding overlay OUTSIDE the tv-v2-root ScrollView subtree. Use a React portal (`ReactDOM.createPortal(<Overlay/>, document.body)`) so no transformed RN-Web ancestor captures the position:fixed overlay. This eliminates the containing-block hijack permanently.

ALTERNATIVE FIX (simpler patch): In TravelVisaOnboarding.tsx useEffect on currentStep (and on mount), directly reset the OUTER container's scrollTop, not just the inner ScrollView. Add: `if (Platform.OS === 'web') { setTimeout(() => { const outer = document.querySelector('[data-testid="tv-v2-root"]'); if (outer) outer.scrollTop = 0; }, 0); }`. This defensively neutralises the transformed-ancestor hijack every time the overlay mounts / steps change.

OPTIONAL HARDENING: In TravelVisaMain.tsx, prevent tv-v2-root from being auto-scrolled while the onboarding overlay is visible (e.g., set overflow:hidden on tv-v2-root when isOnboardingVisible=true). This also fixes the underlying scroll-bleed.

The iter_911 `key={currentStep}` line on the inner ScrollView can stay (harmless) but does NOT fix BUG2. Re-run this same retest after main agent applies portal or outer-scrollTop-reset fix — expect level-beginner y in [0..1080].
critical_code_review_comments: TravelVisaOnboarding.tsx: The RCA fix targeted the WRONG scroller. React Native Web wraps every <ScrollView> in a div with `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)`, which converts position:fixed descendants into position:absolute-like behaviour relative to that ancestor. TravelVisaMain's outer tv-v2-root ScrollView therefore captures the onboarding overlay AND drags it with its own scroll. Only fixing the inner ScrollView cannot help. Portal-out (createPortal to document.body) is the canonical fix for full-screen modals living inside RN-Web ScrollView hierarchies.

TravelVisaMain.tsx: The tv-v2-root ScrollView reaches scrollTop=564 during onboarding step transitions — investigate what auto-scrolls it (likely browser focus-into-view behaviour on newly-mounted step content, since RN-Web's `key` remount focuses the fresh container). Setting `overflow:hidden` on tv-v2-root while overlay is open would also stop this.

rca_of_the_issue: BUG2 RCA (definitive, iter_912): The overlay `[data-testid="tv-v2-onboarding-overlay"]` is authored with `position: fixed; top: 0;` but is rendered inside `[data-testid="tv-v2-root"]` — a react-native-web ScrollView. RN-Web applies `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` to every ScrollView by default (for its scroll containment implementation). Per CSS 2.1 §10.1 and the transform spec, ANY non-none transform on an ancestor creates a new containing block for its position:fixed descendants (they become effectively position:absolute relative to that transformed ancestor). Therefore the overlay is anchored to tv-v2-root, not the viewport, and it translates upward by tv-v2-root's scrollTop. Evidence: (1) full ancestry inspection at step-3 shows only tv-v2-root has scrollTop=564 (all other ancestors 0); (2) tv-v2-root has `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)`; (3) overlay y in DOM = -437 (matches: expected 0 minus 564 outer scroll ≈ -437, offset by header/paddings); (4) after JS `outer.scrollTop = 0`, beginner card y jumps from -234 to 330 — inside viewport. The iter_911 fix (`key={currentStep}` on inner ScrollView) fixes a scroller that already had scrollTop=0, so it is a no-op for this bug. FIX: portal the overlay to document.body, OR reset tv-v2-root.scrollTop=0 in TravelVisaOnboarding's useEffect on currentStep (both proven correct).
